# `scss/at-function-named-arguments`

**Function arguments are passed by name**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-scss` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-scss` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does (auto when the function is defined in the same file, whose parameter names the edit writes; otherwise reported without an edit) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `stylelint-scss/at-function-named-arguments` |

## What it checks

A call to a `@function` passes its arguments by name: `size($base: 2)`.

**Why:** A named argument says what it is, and survives a reordered signature.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-scss
pip install codelaw-rules-scss
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:scss/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:scss/recommended"]

[rules]
"scss/at-function-named-arguments" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"scss/at-function-named-arguments" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.scss"]
rules = { "scss/at-function-named-arguments" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"scss/at-function-named-arguments" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"scss/at-function-named-arguments" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"scss/at-function-named-arguments" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "scss/at-function-named-arguments": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore scss/at-function-named-arguments: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore scss/at-function-named-arguments expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule scss/at-function-named-arguments --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain scss/at-function-named-arguments       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule scss/at-function-named-arguments  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                    # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
@function size($base) {
  @return $base * 2;
}
a {
  width: size(2px);
}
```

#### Do

```scss
@function size($base) {
  @return $base * 2;
}
a {
  width: size($base: 2px);
}
```
